provenance.validation_note: The official LUNA-OPS validation report covers the science engine (backend/lunaops) only. This screening package is outside that fingerprint and has not been validated.

dem.product: PGDA 90: A New View of the Lunar South Pole from LOLA - LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ
dem.citation: Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole
dem.crs: south polar stereographic on the 1737.4 km sphere (true scale at the pole), metres
dem.vertical: height in metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere

error_map.product: LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ_ERR.TIF (255 MB): LDEM surface height error in metres
error_map.units: m (RMS height uncertainty, declared by product)

algorithms.slope: Horn (1981) 3 x 3 weighted finite differences; spacing = pixel / k x (R + h) / R, k = projection point scale; NaN if any of the 9 samples is missing
algorithms.roughness: RMS of residuals about the least-squares plane in a 5 x 5 window (complete windows only)
algorithms.tri: Terrain Ruggedness Index, Riley et al. (1999): sqrt of the sum of squared differences to the 8 neighbours
algorithms.depressions: Priority-Flood depression filling (Barnes et al. 2014) seeded at the window edge and next to missing data; 8-connected regions deeper than the configured minimum depth below their spill level; size from area-equivalent diameter; shape from second moments

depression_quality.defined: depth >= 3 x mean RMS height uncertainty in the region, axis ratio >= 0.5, ellipse fill >= 0.6
depression_quality.shape_only: no error map: depth cannot be compared with uncertainty
depression_quality.note: LUNA-OPS landing 0.1.0 screening convention, not a published criterion

limitations: Preliminary screening only: no result certifies a landing site as safe.
Slope and roughness describe the DEM at its pixel scale; LOLA 5 m products are mostly interpolated between laser tracks, so their effective resolution is coarser than the pixel size.
DEM roughness is not rock or boulder detection.

Depression candidates are unconfirmed; they are not identified as impact craters. Depth is counted only below the level at which a hollow could drain to the window edge or to missing data, so hollows open to the edge or to a data gap, and depressions breached on slopes, are missed or measured shallower.
Depth is measured below the spill level (lowest rim point), not from the rim crest.
Thresholds are user-defined assumptions; no default or published landing limit is applied.

No imagery-based obstacle product is registered. This screening uses 80 m DEM pixels, and even the finest registered LOLA product (PGDA 78, 5 m pixels, about 90% of them interpolated between laser tracks) cannot resolve boulders or other metre-scale obstacles. Orbital imagery review is required; even then orbital data cannot guarantee that every landing hazard is found.
